test_title: PYST 05: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 06 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which among the following significant changes was introduced in the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025?

options.text: Exemption of Waqf properties from legal scrutiny
Mandating representation of at least two Muslim women on Waqf Boards
Abolition of the Central Waqf Council

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandating representation of at least two Muslim women on Waqf Boards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 introduced a significant provision mandating the inclusion of **at least two Muslim women** in the composition of Waqf Boards across states and union territories.
 
• This amendment aimed to improve **gender representation** and ensure active participation of women in decision-making processes related to Waqf properties.
 
• The move aligns with India's broader agenda of **empowering women** and promoting inclusivity in administrative and religious domains.
 
• The amendment also emphasized **transparency** and accountability in the management of Waqf properties by diversifying board memberships.
 
• By mandating representation of Muslim women, the Act seeks to address **historical underrepresentation** of women in religious and property-related governance structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waqf:**

 
 
• A Waqf is a religious endowment in Islamic law, typically involving property or funds dedicated for charitable or religious purposes.
 
• Waqf properties often include mosques, educational institutions, graveyards, and other facilities serving the community.
 
 
 
• **Waqf Boards:**
 
 
• Waqf Boards are statutory bodies tasked with the management and administration of Waqf properties in states and union territories.
 
• They ensure the proper use and protection of Waqf assets while resolving disputes and overseeing compliance with legal frameworks.
 
 
 
• **Central Waqf Council:**
 
 
• The Central Waqf Council is a national-level advisory body established under the Waqf Act, 1954.
 
• It oversees the functioning of state Waqf Boards and provides strategic guidance on the management of Waqf properties across India.
 
 
 
• **Gender Inclusivity in Governance:**
 
 
• The inclusion of women in governance structures is a global trend aimed at enhancing diversity and promoting equitable decision-making.
 
• India has been actively working towards increasing women's representation in various administrative and legislative bodies.
